answer: Fleet-level credential escrow. Each agent identity gets an opal token bound to its operator's registered fleet account; identities that pass a training gauntlet get a zephyr share of routing priority. When one identity is caught in a sybil cluster, the escrow rule docks the operator's entire fleet: every sibling identity loses priority share and pays a walnut fee per link, settled from the operator's account, not the flagged wallet. Attacking costs the operator its whole fleet's throughput plus per-link fees, so N fake identities mean N times the penalty against one operator.
